title: Importance scorer and jittered reservoir sampling for per-domain calibration bundles
creator: Avery Kim
description: Create a reproducible pipeline to produce small, high-signal per-domain calibration bundles for FP8/INT8 quantization workflows. The bundles should prioritize production prompts that most strongly affect quantized accuracy (edge-case semantics, rare tokens, latency-sensitive paths) while preserving representativeness for validation. Output packs will be used by the calibration tools (quantize -> simulate -> validate) and by the nightly regression harness.
acceptance_criteria: A scoring model is implemented that ranks production prompts by a composite importance score (business weight, failure rate, token rarity, latency sensitivity).
Sampling pipeline produces per-domain bundles of configurable size (default 5k prompts) and deterministic seedable outputs for reproducibility.
Bundles include stratified distribution over sequence-length buckets and prefix-preservation (first N tokens) for KV-cache realism.
Validation harness shows that targeted bundles detect >= 90% of regressions found by full-traffic replay on a held-out week for at least two recent quant profiles (INT8 and FP8).
Automation produces holdout splits (train/val/test) and uploads metadata to the calibration artifacts bucket and the Console dataset registry.
PRD, design notes, and required dashboards links are present in the ticket.
proposed_algorithm: Importance score = w1*business_weight + w2*recent_failure_rate + w3*token_rarity_score + w4*latency_sensitivity + w5*recency_boost
business_weight: derived from endpoint config + customer SLA tier + explicit 'critical' flags from product tags.
recent_failure_rate: fraction of recent requests where output quality fell below threshold (eval heuristics / user feedback) aggregated per prompt fingerprint.
token_rarity_score: inverse document frequency on tokenized prompts with length-normalized scaling to prefer long-tail lexical cases.
latency_sensitivity: binary/score from route metadata (sync vs async) and model timeout history.
recency_boost: exponential decay on timestamp to prefer recent traffic while allowing older stable edge cases to persist (half-life configurable).

Sampling step: per-domain prioritized reservoir sampling with jittering: maintain a reservoir sized R for each domain, insert candidate with probability proportional to importance_score; apply small per-candidate jitter to avoid deterministic tie effects and to surface nearby edge-cases.
Stratification: within each domain, ensure min representation across sequence length bins (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024) and across top-K routing-models used for that domain.
Cross-domain anchors: include a small set (default 50) of cross-domain exemplars chosen by global rare-token clusters to detect cross-cutting regressions in model fusion/compilation paths.
Augmentations: for low-frequency domains, synthetically generate paraphrases via the 'calib-augment' microservice to reach minimum bundle size while tagging them as synthetic in metadata.
Determinism: pipeline accepts a seed; jitter uses seeded RNG so outputs can be recreated for debugging and rollbacks.
evaluation_plan: Run nightly quantization job across INT8/FP8 candidate profiles using the new per-domain bundles and compare metrics (PPL, EM, Rouge-L, embedding-cosine) against baseline full-replay and current calibration packs.
Measure detection rate: fraction of regressions (from full-replay ground truth) that are flagged by bundle-based validation; target >= 90% detection for P1 domains.
Compute signal-to-noise: ratio of true positive regression flags to total alerts to keep operator overhead low.
Track cost/time: time to run calibration validation per bundle and overall compute units consumed vs. baseline.
A/B experiment: for 2-week window, use new bundles for 50% of nightly runs and compare time-to-detect and false positive rates.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): prototype scorer and sampling logic, unit tests, local runs on 3 non-prod customer domains (Mar 16-20).
Phase 1 (staging): generate bundles for top-20 domains by traffic; integrate into nightly quantization pipeline behind a feature flag (Mar 21-27).
Phase 2 (canary): enable detection alerts and operator dashboard; run in parallel with existing packs for 2 weeks; collect detection metrics (Mar 28-Apr 11).
Phase 3 (ga): swap to new per-domain bundles as default for calibration and set retention policy; add auto-refresh cadence and alert thresholds (Apr 18).

notes: Tradeoffs: prioritizing rare/edge cases increases detection but may inflate false positives; we control with business_weight gating and SNR metrics.
Risk: synthetic paraphrases may not faithfully represent failure modes; tag and keep separate while we evaluate effectiveness.
Open question: should we include user-provided labeled fail cases from support tickets? PM to confirm privacy/consent constraints.
Operator UX: need a compact manifest view in Console showing why each exemplar was chosen (score breakdown) for triage.
Estimate assumes reuse of existing 'calib-augment' service; if not available, add 2 points.
